Animations start one level lower, because the top level tilted and scaled the whole page on every page change and two browsers showed that in two different ways.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The green flash and the trembling page were the same bug** ([#228](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/228)). "Wild" does more than enlarge the animations that were already there: on every page change it tilts the whole page 1.2 degrees and scales it to 96% while travelling 18px, and the cards inside slide in separately on top of that. Transforms nested that way each get their own compositing layer. On Firefox/macOS the coloured badges painted out of layer memory that had not been initialised, which is where the `#38FF38` green came from, and it jumped rather than faded because there was nothing in between to interpolate. Chromium allocates those layers differently and got the colour right, so there the same doubling showed up as the page trembling before it settled.
- **Animations now start at "Subtle".** The entrance stays at 6px with no tilt and no scale, which leaves no nested transforms to flash or wobble. Nobody had chosen the top level: it was simply what shipped, on the reasoning that this setting only ever makes existing animations quicker or smaller. Tilting and scaling the page is where that reasoning stopped holding. **Wild** is unchanged and still available under Settings, General, Animations.
- **A strong-level choice made before the setting was renamed is carried over** rather than reset. While the default was the strong level, an old stored value fell through to a default that happened to be the same level, so nothing was lost. Moving the default ends that coincidence, and without this an earlier deliberate choice would have been quietly downgraded.

## 🔍 Not verified here

- The green flash was traced in the code and from the reporter's two recordings, not reproduced: there is no macOS machine with Firefox on this side. The nesting and the level's values are measured; that this particular engine stops flashing is a conclusion drawn from them.
